_notes: Verdicts for shacl/cases.json on @factoidal/core 0.16.0, written by tools/echo04-study/shacl-triage.mjs. One group per cause; groups lists each group's evidence once. issue "NEW:<group>" marks a defect not yet filed.

anon-bnode-label.spec: SPARQL 1.1 Update section 3.1.1 (INSERT DATA; blank nodes in QuadData) and RDF 1.2 N-Quads grammar BLANK_NODE_LABEL (https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-n-quads/#sec-grammar)
anon-bnode-label.note: shaclValidate(data) rejects a Dataset whose blank nodes were made by [] in INSERT DATA: the engine writes them as _:b_d__:bnode_N (a colon inside the label) and its own N-Quads reader rejects the text (parse.syntax "expected '.' terminator" or "expected '<' (IRIREF)"). Dataset.query CONSTRUCT over the same store rejects the same way. Labelled blank nodes (_:x) are fine. Same family as danbri/factoidal#740 / #742 (742, CONSTRUCT template labels, closed); this path is not fixed in 0.16.0.

sparql-boolean-dot.spec: SPARQL 1.1 Query section 19.8 grammar: [134] BooleanLiteral ::= 'true' | 'false'; [140] PNAME_NS ::= PN_PREFIX? ':' (a prefixed name needs a colon; PN_PREFIX [168] cannot end in '.')
sparql-boolean-dot.note:
The SPARQL lexer reads `true.` / `false.` (boolean literal directly followed by the triple terminator) as a prefixed name: INSERT DATA {

true. } is an update.syntax error, and a query FILTER(true.) reports "unresolved prefix: true.". `true .` (with a space) and `1.` are read correctly.

deactivated-nested.spec: SHACL 2017 section 2.1.6 Deactivating a Shape (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#deactivated): "A shape that has the value true for the property sh:deactivated is called deactivated. All RDF terms conform to a deactivated shape."
deactivated-nested.note: A deactivated shape used as a member of sh:or (or as the value of sh:not) is treated as a shape nothing conforms to: sh:or ( [ sh:class ex:B ; sh:deactivated true ] ) reports a violation, sh:not [ ...deactivated... ] conforms. A deactivated shape at sh:node is handled correctly.

languageIn-wildcard.spec: SHACL 2017 section 4.4.4 sh:languageIn (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#LanguageInConstraintComponent): value nodes must have "a language tag matching any of the basic language ranges ... following the filtering schema defined by the SPARQL langMatches function"; SPARQL 1.1 Query 17.4.3.12 langMatches and RFC 4647 section 2.1: the basic language range "*" matches every non-empty tag
languageIn-wildcard.note: sh:languageIn ( "*" ) reports a violation for "x"@en; RDF4J (and langMatches) accept every language-tagged literal.

sparql-nested.spec: SHACL 2017 section 5.3 Validation with SPARQL-based Constraints and section 4.7.2 sh:property / 4.6.1 sh:not (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#sparql-constraints-validation): conformance checking of a value node against a shape includes every constraint of that shape, SPARQL-based ones included
sparql-nested.note: A SPARQL-based constraint (sh:sparql) is evaluated only on a shape that has its own target. On a shape reached through sh:property, sh:node or sh:not it is never evaluated: the property shape conforms (no result), and sh:not [ sh:sparql ... ] always fails.

maxCount-negative.spec: SHACL 2017 section 4.2.2 sh:maxCount (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#MaxCountConstraintComponent): "The values of sh:maxCount in a property shape are literals with datatype xsd:integer." "If the number of value nodes is greater than $maxCount, there is a validation result."
maxCount-negative.note: sh:maxCount -1 never reports a result (0 value nodes > -1). RDF4J reports one. The REC places no lower bound on sh:maxCount (shsh:ShapeShape only requires xsd:integer).

multi-list-param.spec: SHACL 2017 section 2.1.1 Constraints, Parameters and Constraint Components (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#constraints): parameters "may be used multiple times in the same shape, and each value of such a parameter declares an individual constraint. The interpretation of such declarations is conjunction"; section 4.6.3 sh:or: "Each value of sh:or in a shape is a SHACL list."
multi-list-param.note: A shape with two sh:or lists (or two sh:and lists) is checked against the first value only: sh:or ( [sh:class ex:A] ), ( [sh:class ex:B] ) conforms for a node of type ex:A only. Two sh:class values are handled correctly.

rsx-targetShape.spec: SHACL 2017 section 2.1.3 Targets (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#targets): the targets of a shape are sh:targetNode, sh:targetClass, implicit class targets, sh:targetSubjectsOf and sh:targetObjectsOf. rsx:targetShape is an RDF4J extension (RSX, enabled by setEclipseRdf4jShaclExtensions(true))
rsx-targetShape.note: Factoidal reads no rsx:targetShape, so the shape has no focus nodes and the data conforms; RDF4J targets the nodes that conform to the target shape.

dash-hasValueIn.spec: SHACL 2017 section 4 Core Constraint Components (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#core-components): dash:hasValueIn is not a SHACL constraint component; it is a DASH (TopBraid) extension that RDF4J enables with setDashDataShapes(true)
dash-hasValueIn.note: Factoidal ignores dash:hasValueIn, so the shape that carries it has no constraint (conforms where RDF4J expects a violation, and fails under sh:not where RDF4J expects conformance).

dash-target.spec: SHACL 2017 section 2.1.3 Targets (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#targets) does not define sh:target; sh:target is the SHACL Advanced Features (W3C Working Group Note 2017) section 5 custom target, and dash:AllObjectsTarget / dash:AllSubjectsTarget are DASH target types
dash-target.note: core.shaclValidate rejects a shapes graph that uses sh:target (validate.failed: "the shapes graph uses a feature this validator does not read: sh:target (SPARQL-based targets)"), as its API documents; RDF4J reads DASH all-objects / all-subjects targets.

shacl-af-sparql-target.spec: SHACL Advanced Features (W3C Working Group Note 2017) section 5.1 SPARQL-based Targets (https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl-af/#SPARQLTarget); not part of SHACL 2017 section 2.1.3 Targets (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#targets)
shacl-af-sparql-target.note: core.shaclValidate rejects shapes graphs with sh:target / sh:SPARQLTarget by design (index.d.ts: "A shapes graph that uses the SPARQL-based target of SHACL-AF ... reject"). Divergence, not gap: the feature is outside the SHACL Recommendation, and rule 1 keeps it out of the echo. Under the SHACL 1.2 SPARQL Extensions draft, which carries SPARQL-based targets, it would become an engine coverage item.

shapes-graph-subclass.spec: SHACL 2017 section 1.1 (SHACL subclass, SHACL instance are defined "in the data graph") and section 2.1.3.2 (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#targetClass): "all the rdfs:subClassOf declarations needed to walk the class hierarchy need to exist in the data graph"
shapes-graph-subclass.note: The rdfs:subClassOf triples of this case are in the shapes graph only; RDF4J (with its RDFS subclass reasoner) uses them for sh:class and sh:targetClass, Factoidal follows the REC and does not.

shacl12-defaultValue.spec: SHACL 2017 section 2.3.2.4 sh:defaultValue (https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-shacl-20170720/#defaultValue): non-validating, "ignored by SHACL processors"; SHACL 1.2 Core (Editor's Draft) section Value Nodes of Property Shapes (https://w3c.github.io/data-shapes/shacl12-core/#value-nodes-property-shapes): "If the set is still empty and d is the value of sh:defaultValue ... add the output nodes"
shacl12-defaultValue.note: Factoidal follows the SHACL 1.2 Core draft: a property shape with no values takes sh:defaultValue as its value node (here ex:iri1, which is not an ex:Person, so sh:class reports it). RDF4J follows SHACL 2017, where sh:defaultValue does not take part in validation. The two specification versions disagree; the RDF4J expectation is right under the Recommendation.

rdf4j-update-graph-syntax.spec: SPARQL 1.1 Query section 19.8 grammar [52] QuadsNotTriples ::= 'GRAPH' VarOrIri '{' TriplesTemplate? '}' (used by SPARQL 1.1 Update section 3.1.1 INSERT DATA)
rdf4j-update-graph-syntax.note: The case's update writes ex:dataGraph { ... } inside INSERT DATA without the GRAPH keyword (TriG style). RDF4J's parser accepts it; it is not SPARQL 1.1, and Factoidal rejects it (update.syntax).
